policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Word order only: 'no one can do these signs' renders the same words either way, and English syntax fixes its own order. Nothing in the ASV distinguishes delta-y-n-a-t-a-i before or after the object phrase; no note is mapped here.

Presence or absence of the article with the name is invisible in English: 'Jesus answered' renders both. The only note on the verse is an alternative_rendering on 'anew/from above', which cannot decide a reading.
Article with the proper name; 'Nicodemus saith unto him' is the same English with or without it, and no note is mapped here.
Article with the name; 'Jesus answered' renders both readings identically and no note is mapped here.

The ASV prints 'even the Son of man, who is in heaven', rendering the added clause; the mapped note 'Man ancient authorities omit who is in heaven' confirms the longer text is what the translators set and the omission is the variant.

The ASV reads 'that whosoever believeth may in him have eternal life' — 'in him' construed with 'have', and no 'should not perish, but' before it. The RP reading supplies exactly that clause, so the ASV's shorter wording excludes it; the note is an alternative_rendering about where 'in him' attaches and does not bear on the variant.
The ASV reads 'he gave his only begotten Son', with an unitalicized possessive; the ASV italicizes supplied words, so 'his' renders the added pronoun rather than the bare article.
The ASV reads 'God sent not the Son into the world' — the definite article and no possessive, so the added pronoun of the longer reading is unrendered.

The ASV opens the verse 'He that believeth on him is not judged' with no connective; the ASV routinely leaves this particle untranslated, so its absence in English does not distinguish presence from omission, and no note is mapped here.
Word order of pronoun and adjective only: 'their works were evil' is the same English either way, and no note is mapped here.
Article with the name; 'And John also was baptizing' renders both. The verse's only note is a greek_gloss on 'much water' and does not touch this unit.
Article with the name; 'For John was not yet cast into prison' is identical with or without it, and no note is mapped here.
Both readings mean 'nothing'; the ASV's plain 'can receive nothing' adds no emphatic 'not even one thing' that would mark the two-word form, and no note is mapped here.
The ASV reads 'Ye yourselves bear me witness': the dative pronoun is rendered by 'me', which the omitting reading has nothing to supply.

The ASV has 'that I said, I am not the Christ'. The emphatic pronoun would be absorbed by the English verb's own subject, and a recitative conjunction before direct speech is represented by the comma rather than a word, so none of the three readings is distinguished; no note is mapped here.
The ASV begins the verse 'What he hath seen and heard' with no coordinating 'and', so the added conjunction of the longer reading is unrendered.
The ASV reads 'for he giveth not the Spirit by measure', keeping the pronoun subject; the longer reading names God as the explicit subject, which the ASV does not render here.
